title: Shared & Core Modules 🤝
description: Prevent duplication with SharedModule and keep singleton services safe in CoreModule.

slides.title: The Problem of Repetition 🔁
slides.content:
# Why Shared and Core Modules?

In a multi‑module app, you’ll often import the same stuff everywhere (e.g., `CommonModule`, `FormsModule`, custom components).

This leads to:
* Duplicated imports.
* Accidental re‑providing of services, creating multiple instances.

Angular style guide recommends two special modules:
* **SharedModule** – re‑exports commonly used directives, pipes, and components.
* **CoreModule** – holds singleton services and app‑wide components (like header/footer).

slides.title: SharedModule Example

quizData.question: What is the primary purpose of a SharedModule?

options.text: To re‑export commonly used components, directives, and pipes.

quizData.explanation: SharedModule collects and re‑exports frequently used items so other modules only import it.

CoreModule Example
slides.content: Collect global services and single‑use components:

slides.title: Don't Import Shared Module into Core Module ⚠️
slides.content: If `CoreModule` imports `SharedModule`, then every feature module that imports `SharedModule` will indirectly get the services from `CoreModule`? No – services are not imported via modules. But it’s cleaner to keep CoreModule focused on singleton providers and app‑wide components, not shared widgets.

quizData.question: A service provided in CoreModule will be a singleton if CoreModule is imported only in AppModule.
quizData.explanation: Yes, the root module injector creates one instance that is shared app‑wide.
